payload.question_text: A healthcare diagnostic app uses medical images. The app service needs a stored key, but doctors need different access to model data. Which approach should set the doctors' permissions?

options.error_type: Confuses employee permissions with secret storage
options.rationale: Key Vault stores the application's key as a secret. It does not assign different permissions to doctors.
options.better_fit: Use Key Vault to keep the app service's key out of code and GitHub.

feedback.intrinsic: The key could be protected, but doctors would not receive the needed access levels.
feedback.instructional: Protect keys in Key Vault; assign people permissions with Entra ID and RBAC.

options.rationale: Doctors need permissions that differ by role. Entra ID with RBAC limits access to data and resources according to assigned roles.

options.error_type: Confuses application identity with user role permissions
options.rationale: A managed identity lets the app retrieve a secret securely at runtime. It does not set doctors' role-based access to data.
options.better_fit: Use a managed identity when the app service retrieves its stored key from Key Vault.

feedback.intrinsic: The application could get its key, while doctor permissions would remain unset.
feedback.instructional: Managed identity serves the application; RBAC serves role-based permissions.

options.error_type: Confuses endpoint authentication with role-based authorization
options.rationale: An API key authenticates a request to an endpoint. It does not give different doctors different data permissions.
options.better_fit: Use an API key when an application calls an endpoint and must authenticate that call.

feedback.intrinsic: One key would not separate doctors by their assigned access.
feedback.instructional: A key authenticates a call. RBAC authorizes access by role.

payload.explanation: Correct. Doctors' different permissions should be assigned through Entra ID with RBAC.

payload.question_text: A finance company must keep real-time transaction data available across global locations. Which choices best fit this need? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Azure Cosmos DB supports real-time globally distributed data. That matches transaction data needed across global locations.

options.error_type: Confuses mission-critical workloads with global real-time data
options.rationale: Azure SQL Database is described for mission-critical workloads. Azure Cosmos DB is the option described for real-time globally distributed data.
options.better_fit: Choose Azure SQL Database when the key requirement is a mission-critical workload.

feedback.intrinsic: The company could overlook the storage option identified for real-time global distribution.
feedback.instructional: For real-time data across global locations, select Azure Cosmos DB and persistent storage.

options.rationale: Persistent storage keeps information available for later use. The company needs transaction data to remain available across locations.
Real-time global distribution is the capability described for Azure Cosmos DB. It directly matches the stated availability need.

payload.explanation: Correct. Azure Cosmos DB with persistent storage and real-time global distribution fits this transaction-data requirement.

payload.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A capacity change could be planned in the wrong direction.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Remember the pairing: scale out adds instances, and scale up adds CPU or memory to an existing instance.

payload.correct_answer: Scale out adds more instances while scale up adds CPU or memory
payload.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds running copies, while vertical scaling gives an existing copy more CPU or memory. These choices address different capacity needs.

payload.question_text: A manufacturing team packages its predictive-maintenance workloads as many containers. It needs one service to manage those workloads together. Which choice best fits?

options.error_type: Confuses container orchestration with web app hosting
options.rationale: App Service hosts web apps, APIs, and background jobs. It is not the service described for orchestrating many containers.
options.better_fit: Use App Service when quickly hosting a web app, API, or background job.

feedback.intrinsic: The containers would not be managed by the service intended for large container workloads.
feedback.instructional: Choose AKS when the central need is orchestrating many containers.

options.error_type: Confuses capacity adjustment with workload orchestration
options.rationale: Scale out adds more app instances. It does not manage a collection of containerized workloads.
options.better_fit: Use scale out when request volume requires additional app copies.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could add copies without organizing its container workloads.
feedback.instructional: Scaling changes capacity; AKS orchestrates containers.

options.error_type: Confuses a host environment with a container orchestrator
options.rationale: A virtual machine is a host that provides compute, memory, and networking. It is not the service that orchestrates many containers.
options.better_fit: Use a virtual machine when an application needs a cloud host environment.

feedback.intrinsic: The workloads would have a host, but no orchestrator for managing them together.
feedback.instructional: A VM is a host. AKS manages large numbers of containerized workloads.

options.rationale: AKS orchestrates many containerized workloads. That directly matches a team that needs to manage many containers together.

payload.explanation: Correct. AKS is the Azure service for orchestrating many containerized workloads.

payload.question_text: A finance fraud-detection service has one busy app instance. Its engineer wants that same instance to have more processing power, not more copies. Which choices fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Scale up is vertical scaling of an existing instance. It matches the requirement for more power without more copies.
Scale up increases CPU or memory on an existing instance. More CPU gives that same copy more processing capacity.
More memory is another form of scale up. It changes resources on the existing instance rather than adding copies.

options.error_type: Confuses vertical scaling with horizontal scaling
options.rationale: Scale out adds more instances. The engineer specifically wants to keep one instance and increase its resources.
options.better_fit: Use scale out when additional copies of the application are wanted.

feedback.intrinsic: The service would gain more copies, contrary to the engineer's stated need.
feedback.instructional: Choose scale up for more CPU or memory on one existing instance.

payload.explanation: Correct. Scale up increases CPU or memory on the existing instance without adding copies.

payload.question_text: An application can securely retrieve a secret at runtime by using a ___.

parts.text: An application can securely retrieve a secret at runtime by using a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The app would not have the secure retrieval method needed for its stored secret.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use managed identity to retrieve a Key Vault secret. Entra ID and RBAC manage access, while an API key authenticates an endpoint request.

payload.explanation: A managed identity is the secure identity an application uses to retrieve a stored secret at runtime.
